title: Recall Quiz: Later Romantics: Coleridge, Byron, Shelley, Keats, Austen

questions.q: Which Romantic writer coined the phrase 'willing suspension of disbelief' in his prose work Biographia Literaria?
questions.explanation: Coleridge used this phrase to describe how readers should approach supernatural elements in poetry.

questions.q: Percy Bysshe Shelley's 'Adonais' is a pastoral elegy mourning the death of:
questions.explanation: Shelley wrote Adonais to mourn the tragic early death of Keats.

questions.q: John Keats coined which term to describe the capacity to remain in doubts and uncertainties without reaching after fact and reason?
questions.explanation: He used 'Negative Capability' to praise Shakespeare's objective, open-minded genius.

questions.q: Jane Austen's novels, such as 'Pride and Prejudice', are best classified as:
questions.explanation: She perfected the Novel of Manners, focusing on social behavior and courtship.

questions.q: Which poem contains the famous lines 'Water, water, every where, / Nor any drop to drink'?
options: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
questions.explanation: These lines are spoken by the cursed sailor in Coleridge's masterpiece.

questions.q: Lord Byron's masterpiece, a massive satirical epic that reverses a famous legend to make its hero an innocent man seduced by women, is:
questions.explanation: Don Juan is Byron's greatest and most humorous satirical work.

questions.q: Who wrote the line 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty'?
questions.explanation: This is the concluding philosophical statement of Keats's 'Ode on a Grecian Urn'.

questions.q: Which poem by Shelley describes the shattered statue of an ancient king in the desert, symbolizing the inevitable decay of tyrannical power?
questions.explanation: Ozymandias is a famous sonnet warning against the hubris of absolute rulers.
